history.summary: A small shrine on the north side of the Kumbha Shyam (Varaha) temple complex inside Chittorgarh Fort, dedicated to the bhakti saint Meera Bai and her deity Krishna, built in Indo-Aryan style with the distinctive 'five bodies, one head' carving (symbolising spiritual equality across castes) and a chhatri marking the footprints of Meera's guru Raidas. CHRONOLOGY CONFLICT: travel sources say Rana Kumbha built it for Meera, but Kumbha died in 1468 while Meera Bai (1498-1546) lived in the 16th century, so the attribution is chronologically inconsistent - the shrine may have been renamed/dedicated to her later. Coordinates are approximate (complex-level; the geocoder resolves both Meera Temple and Kumbha Shyam Temple to the same complex point).

name: Meera Temple
town_description: Chittorgarh, former capital of the Sisodia dynasty of Mewar, is dominated by its massive hill fort (a UNESCO World Heritage site), the largest fort in India, revered as a symbol of Rajput valour, sacrifice and devotion.

travel.railway: Chittorgarh Junction (~6 km from the fort); the fort is about 350 m from the temple complex
travel.road: The fort sits on a hill ~2 km south of Chittorgarh town, reached by a winding 1 km road

visitor_information.opening_hours: Fort complex typically 6:00 AM-6:00 PM (fort entry ticket applies; ASI ticket Rs 10 Indian / Rs 100 foreign reported - verify)
